items.headline: Merck and Moderna’s melanoma vaccine data bring adoption test into focus
items.preview: Merck and Moderna's personalized cancer vaccine shows promise in melanoma treatment.
items.article:
Merck and Moderna’s personalized cancer vaccine has demonstrated benefit beyond adjuvant Keytruda in melanoma. The commercial question is whether those gains are enough to justify the anticipated cost and manufacturing complexity of a bespoke therapy as other immunotherapy strategies expand patients’ treatment options.
Adding intismeran autogene to Keytruda pembrolizumab reduced the risk of recurrence or death by 42% in Phase III (HR=0.58; p<0.001), marking a milestone for personalized cancer vaccines. But its place in melanoma care could also depend on how the regimen compares with approaches that start immunotherapy before surgery—a question the trial did not address.
Why this matters: The results could influence treatment decisions and the future of personalized cancer vaccines in the competitive landscape of melanoma therapies.

items.headline: Roche scraps off-the-shelf CAR-T from Poseida deal worth up to $1.5B
items.preview: Roche discontinues RG6540 CAR-T therapy, citing better alternatives.
items.article:
Roche has discontinued RG6540, an experimental off-the-shelf CAR-T therapy targeting the CD19 and CD20 proteins, less than two years after agreeing to acquire its developer, Poseida Therapeutics, for up to $1.5 billion. Roche has not explained the reasons for the decision, but CEO Thomas Schinecker indicated that the acquisition had yielded other CD19/CD20 candidates he considers superior.
Why it matters: The decision raises questions about Roche's remaining payments related to the acquisition and highlights the challenges in developing effective off-the-shelf CAR-T therapies, particularly regarding immune rejection by patients.

items.headline: Neural network predicts three-year local recurrence after lung SBRT with higher accuracy than standard models
items.preview: A neural network outperforms traditional models in predicting lung cancer recurrence.
items.article:
An interpretable artificial neural network can predict whether a lung tumor will return within three years after stereotactic body radiation therapy. The model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.892, outperforming both conventional logistic regression and established radiobiological models.
Why this matters: This advancement could help clinicians better identify patients at elevated risk of local failure after treatment, potentially improving patient outcomes and personalizing therapy approaches.

items.headline: Herbal medicine research against Shigella surges, but hard evidence lags behind
items.preview: Traditional Chinese medicine research on Shigella is growing, but lacks rigorous trials.
items.article:
Research on traditional Chinese medicine for bacillary dysentery has entered a phase of explosive growth, yet the field still lacks rigorous clinical trials and Shigella-specific animal models. A bibliometric analysis revealed a significant increase in publications, particularly after 2021, driven by the global crisis of antimicrobial resistance.
Why this matters: Despite the promising growth in research, the lack of strong clinical evidence and standardized trials limits the potential for herbal remedies to be integrated into medical practice against drug-resistant Shigella.

items.headline: High-resolution paleobiome reconstructions highlight ecological and historical dynamics underpinning global terrestrial vertebrate diversity
items.preview: New paleobiome reconstructions reveal insights into biodiversity patterns.
items.article:
This study reconstructs global biome histories for the Cenozoic by downscaling paleoclimate simulations. It finds that present-day biome area and energy are better predictors of vertebrate diversity than historical measures, suggesting biodiversity tracks ecological limits set by shifting biomes.
Why this matters: Understanding the historical drivers of biodiversity can inform conservation efforts and predict how species may respond to future climate changes.
